annotation.kind: audit-driven reconstruction of Theorem 4.1 with an explicit Model-1 execution, algorithm-linked four-source error decomposition, and second-order interpretation of lesssim

assumptions: The matrix dimensions m, n, and q and the word count p are positive.

The input and accumulation formats form a Model-1 binary-format family: accumulation precision and exponent range contain the input format, and the two rounding maps satisfy (2.3)-(2.4) on operations without overflow.

The diagonal row and column scaling factors are positive powers of two satisfying the maximal intervals (3.4a)-(3.4b), with factor 1 for a zero row or column, and every scaled element is bounded by theta=min(fmax,sqrt(Fmax/n)).
The p input words satisfy the input-rounded recurrences (4.29)-(4.30), and the computed matrix retains exactly the accumulation-format products with i+j

The source-derived certificate exposes the reconstructed word sums, exact retained product, omitted tail, and split input/accumulation errors; requires each split to vanish with the matching Model-1 error function; fixes the four contribution formulas; decomposes the actual computed forward error; supplies the four intermediate bounds from (4.18)-(4.28); and classifies the remaining norm as second order.
The precision filter is nontrivial. NaNs and infinities are outside the finite-real model; underflow is modeled and overflow is excluded on the represented operations.

conditions.L: The identical fixed statement and P20 shared files are present; the frozen NumStability library is also present.
conditions.N: The fixed statement and P20 shared files are present; no NumStability artifact is present.

informal_proof: Use the exact error decomposition from (4.18)-(4.28), repeatedly apply the matrix infinity-norm triangle inequality, substitute the four certified component bounds, and absorb the norm of the remaining matrix into the explicitly second-order scalar remainder. Unfold the coefficient definitions for the separate (4.33) comparison.
